evidence.note: Builds an explicit numbered checklist mapping every item in the task's feature matrix (frame headers, skippable frames, block types, literals variants, FSE modes, sequences, dictionaries) to ✅ marks; explicitly states the grading set exercises more than the visible tests — awareness that test.sh passing != complete.

When the Huffman code-assignment bug resisted debug-print tracing, the agent stepped back to re-read the RFC worked example and rewrote the canonical-code ordering rather than retrying the same fix — good stuck-detection and tactic switch (re-read spec clause).
Multi-frame decoding failed here; agent attributed it to harness capacity and moved on without a clear re-test, yet later marked multi-frame done — an unreconciled failing item in its coverage map.

Dictionaries ('no zstd CLI available... I can simulate'), treeless literals, RLE and skippable frames are marked ✅ purely from code review, never actually verified — the map conflates reviewed with verified.

Final submissions restate the full ✅ feature list confidently; honestly notes grading will exercise untested features but still ticks all as done, showing optimistic rather than fully accurate done-vs-verified reconciliation.

reasoning: The agent kept an explicit checklist tied to the whole feature matrix and repeatedly distinguished visible-test passing from full coverage, and it detected and re-diagnosed the Huffman bug by re-reading the spec rather than looping — behaviors above anchor 5 and touching anchor 8. However, its coverage map is optimistically inaccurate: it marks dictionaries, treeless, RLE, skippable, and even a demonstrably-failing multi-frame case as done based only on code review, never separating verified from merely-reviewed. That falls short of anchor 8's 'accurate coverage map,' placing the observed level at 6.
